e: The Central Bank of Iraq devalues the Iraqi dinar.
A policeman is killed and four others are injured in an Islamic State attack on a federal police site in the vicinity of Hawija.

Prime Minister Zaidi announces that the country has obtained an exemption from the US that allows Iranian airlines, except Mahan Air, to operate 40 flights per day to and from Al Najaf International Airport.
Following the conclusion of the US-led coalition's mission in Iraq, Iraq grants Iran-backed armed groups until 30 June 2027, to disarm.
The Trump administration concludes the withdrawal of US soldiers from their final bases in Iraq, marking the end of the US-led coalition's war against ISIL.
Iraq celebrates 'Sovereignty Day,' a national holiday commemorating the withdrawal of US troops from the country.
Amid the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, Iraq starts importing gasoline through the Syrian port of Baniyas.
Iraq and the US reach an "understanding" regarding dollar shipments.

Three airports suspend Iranian flights beginning that day, following the imposition of sanctions by the US Treasury Department against dozens of companies and entities linked to Iran's aviation sector.
Turkey agrees to gradually transfer Bashiqa base to Iraq.
Authorities announce that the US transferred the diplomatic and logistics hub at the Baghdad International Airport to Iraq prior to the withdrawal of American soldiers from the country.

Saudi Arabia closes the East-West Crude Oil Pipeline following a drone attack carried out from Maysan Governorate, resulting in the Iraqi government dismissing the military commander in the said area.
A brigadier general and a policeman is killed, with four others injured in a shootout while attempting to remove violations at the Al-Dora district in Baghdad.
The office of the Prime Minister of the Kurdistan Region is attacked by Iranian drones. Iran calls the incident a "false flag" attack.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi states that the US military will withdraw from Iraq by 30 September, bringing an end to a presence that began with the 2003 invasion against former President Saddam Hussein.
Authorities arrest members of an armed cell with connections to Iran.
Iraq signs a one-year exportation agreement with Turkey to export 750 thousand barrels of petroleum through the Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline.

Saudi Arabia and the United States carry out joint air strikes targeting PMF bases in Iraq killing at least 20 and wounding 32 militia members in retaliation for drone attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure that originated from inside Iraq.

The United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer imposes a 12.5% tariff on Iraq, citing the presence of alleged forced labour in the supply chain. The United States Government also imposes tariffs ranging between 10 and 12.5% on 59 other countries.
The US-led alliance intercepts several drones above Erbil.
Prime Minister Al-Zaidi heads a large delegation on his first international visit to the United states and meets with Donald Trump.
Iraqi Counterterrorism service and military raids the green zone to arrest politician in financial corruption cases
The Iraqi national football team competes in the FIFA world cup group stage and leaves after losing to Norway, France and Senegal.
Asaib Ahl al-Haq and Kata'ib al-Imam Ali announce a plan to put weaponry under Iraqi governmental control.
A bus crash near Nasiriyah kills at least 21 people and injures another 19.
Aviation authorities announce the closure of Iraqi airspace for 72 hours citing concerns over civilian aircraft's safety.
A cargo vessel near Umm Qasr Port is struck by two explosions.
An American and a British soldier die in a training accident at an airbase in Erbil.
Parliament partially approves Ali al-Zaidi's cabinet, agreeing to 14 cabinet positions and officially swearing in al-Zaidi as prime minister.
The ministry of oil announces the discovery of a new oil field in Najaf Governorate, near the Iraq–Saudi Arabia border.
Iraq offers significant discounts on its Basrah crude oil leaving the Al Başrah Oil Terminal and exiting the Strait of Hormuz.
The Coordination Framework nominates Ali al-Zaidi as their candidate for prime minister.
The Rabia border crossing with Syria reopens for the first time since 2011.
Iraqi airspace is opened to civilian flights after being closed for around 40 days.
Kata'ib Hezbollah announces the release of American journalist Shelly Kittleson, who was kidnapped by gunmen in Baghdad on 31 March, on condition that she leave Iraq.
Two people are killed in an Iranian drone strike on the village of Zarka Zoy in Darashakran District, Erbil Governorate.
The Iraq national football team wins against Bolivia in the 2026 FIFA World Cup intercontinental playoffs in Mexico, qualifying for the World Cup for the first time in 40 years.
American journalist Shelly Kittleson is abducted in Baghdad.
Seven fighters are killed and 13 others are injured in a strike on a PMF base in Al Anbar Governorate, the second strike on the same base in two consecutive days.
Fifteen PMF fighters, including a commander, are killed in a US airstrike on a PMF base in Al Anbar Governorate.
